params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}

params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}

params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}

params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}

params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}

params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}

params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.

[81] שארית in Zephaniah 3:13: שְׁאֵרִ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֹֽא־יַעֲשׂ֤וּ עַוְלָה֙ וְלֹֽא־יְדַבְּר֣וּ כָזָ֔ב וְלֹֽא־יִמָּצֵ֥א בְּפִיהֶ֖ם לְשׁ֣וֹן תַּרְמִ֑ית כִּי־הֵ֛מָּה יִרְע֥וּ וְרָבְצ֖וּ וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃ {פ}
(The remnant of IsraelShall do no wrongAnd speak no falsehood;A deceitful tongueShall not be in their mouths.Only such as these shall graze and lie down,With none to trouble them.)
BDB שְׁאֵרִית:
n.f. rest, residue, remnant, remainder (= שָׁאָר);—שׁ׳ abs. 2 S 14:7 +, cstr. Ez 36:3 +, שֵׁרִית (Ges§ 23 f) 1 Ch 12:39 (van d. H. v 38); sf. שְׁאֵרִיתֵךְ Is 14
  rest, what is left, of wood Is 44:17, land 15:9 (‖ פְּלֵיטָה), Je 47:4, 5; Ez 25:16; שׁ׳ חֵמֹת ψ 76:11 is difficult (Gr [cf. Che] proposes חֲמָת Hamath, Du אֻמֹ
  remainder = descendants (= שְׁאָר Is 14:22): Gn 45:7, שֵׁם וּשׁ׳ 2 S 14:7.

[82] לשנים in Proverbs 10:26: כַּחֹ֤מֶץ ׀ לַשִּׁנַּ֗יִם וְכֶעָשָׁ֥ן לָעֵינָ֑יִם כֵּ֥ן הֶ֝עָצֵ֗ל לְשֹׁלְחָֽיו׃
(Like vinegar to the teeth,Like smoke to the eyes,Are sluggards to those who send them on a mission.)
BDB שֵׁן²:
n.f. 1 S 2:13 (yet m. 1 S 14:5 cf. Dr) tooth, ivory;—שׁ׳ abs. Ex 21:24 +, cstr. v 27 +, שֶׁן־ Dt 32:24; sf. שִׁנּוֹ Ex 21:27; du. שִׁנַּיִם Pr 10:26, cstr. שִׁנ
  tooth:
    of man, Ex 21:27(×3) (E), Nu 11:33 (J), Gn 49:12 (poem in J), Am 4:6; Ct 4:2; 6:6, שׁ׳ רֹעָה Pr 25:19, v. II. רעע 2; of lex talionis, שׁ׳ תַּחַת שׁ׳ Ex 21:24 (E
    of beasts: Dt 32:24, crocodile Jb 41:6, locusts Jo 1:6 (teeth of lions); especially fig. of false prophets Mi 3:5, of foes Zc 9:7, oppressors Jb 29:17, wicked 4
    tooth of a fork, tine, 1 S 2:13 (cf. Dr Sm. 291); of cliff, שֵׁן הַסֶּלַע 14:4(×2), cf. Jb 39:28, הַשֵּׁן 1 S 14:5.
  ivory, of commerce, קַרְנוֹת שֵׁן Ez 27:15 (i.e. tusks?); as material, מִטּוֹת שׁ׳ Am 6:4, כִּסֵּא־שׁ׳ 1 K 10:18 = 2 Ch 9:17, בֵּית הָשּׁ׳ 1 K 22:39, cf. Am 3:1

[83] שקר in Exodus 23:7: מִדְּבַר־שֶׁ֖קֶר תִּרְחָ֑ק וְנָקִ֤י וְצַדִּיק֙ אַֽל־תַּהֲרֹ֔ג כִּ֥י לֹא־אַצְדִּ֖יק רָשָֽׁע׃
(Keep far from a false charge; do not bring death on those who are innocent and in the right, for I will not acquit the wrongdoer.)
BDB שֶׁ֫קֶר:
n.m. deception, disappointment, falsehood;—שׁ׳ Ex 23:7 + 64 times; שָׁ֑קֶר Ex 5:9 + 42 times; pl. שְׁקָרִים ψ 101:7 + 3 times; sf. שִׁקְרֵיהֶם Je 23:32;—
  deception,what deceives, disappoints, and betrays one: a molten image Je 10:14 = 51:17; gift Pr 25:14; grace of person 31:30, etc.; אֹ֫רַח שׁ׳ ψ 119:104, 128; ד
  deceit, fraud, wrong: (ל)שׁ׳ עשׂה do or practise fraud, wrong Ho 7:1; Je 6:13; 8:9, 10; c. בְ, 2 S 18:13; פְּעֻלַּת שׁ׳ Pr 11:18; לֶ֫חֶם שׁ׳ Pr 20:17 food got b
  injurious falsehood, in testimony, especially in courts: עֵד שֶׁקֶר Ex 20:16 (E) Dt 19:18 ψ 27:12 Pr 6:19; 14:5; 25:18; עֵד שׁקרים 12:17; 19:5, 9; ענה שׁ׳ Dt 19
  falsity, of false or self-deceived prophets: נבּא שׁ׳ prophesy falsely Je 14:14; 23:25, 26; 29:21; + ל pers. 27:10, 14, 16; נ׳ לַשּׁ׳ v 15; נ׳ בשׁ׳ 5:31; 20:6; 
  lie, falsehood, in gen.: דבר שּׁ׳ ψ 101:7 (‖ רְמִיָּה); דְּבַר שׁ׳ Pr 13:5; of מִלִּים Jb 36:4; לְשׁוֹן שׁ׳ false tongue Pr 6:17; 12:19; 21:6; 26:28; ψ 109:2; o

[84] ישלמנה in Leviticus 24:18: וּמַכֵּ֥ה נֶֽפֶשׁ־בְּהֵמָ֖ה יְשַׁלְּמֶ֑נָּה נֶ֖פֶשׁ תַּ֥חַת נָֽפֶשׁ׃
(One who kills livestock shall make restitution for it: life for life.)
BDB שָׁלֵם:
vb. be complete, sound (NH id. (Jastr), Ph. שלם Pi. complete, requite, especially in n.pr., Lzb 376 GACooke 99, also 81, 111, etc.; Arabic سَلِمَ be safe, secur

    be complete, finished, ended: temple 1 K 7:51 = 2 Ch 5:1; walls of city Ne 6:15; of time Is 60:20.
    be sound, uninjured, Jb 9:4.
  Pf. 3 ms. שִׁלַּם Lv 5:24 +, 1 s. וְשִׁלַּמְתּ֫י Je 16:18 +, etc.; Impf. 3 ms. יְשַׁלֵּם Ex 21:34 +; sf. יְשַׁלְּמֶ֑נָּה Lv 24:18 +, etc.; Imv. ms. שַׁלֵּם Ec 5
    complete, finish, temple 1 K 9:25.
    make safe, c. acc. Jb 8:6.
    make whole or good, restore thing lost Jo 2:25, or stolen Ex 21:37 (E); pay a debt 2 K 4:7 ψ 37:21 Pr 22:27; Jb 41:3; make compensation, for injury Lv 24:18, 21
    make good, i.e. pay, vows, c. acc. נֶדֶר Dt 23:22; 2 S 15:7 + 9 times, + (c. ל to God) ψ 50:14; 66:13; 116:14, 18; obj. om. 76:12; abs. Is 19:21; c. acc. תּוֹדו
    requite, recompense, reward, good 1 S 24:20; Ru 2:12; evil Is 65:6; Je 51:56; c. ל pers. Dt 7:10 + 4 times, + (c. acc. rei) Je 51:24; אל pers. Jb 21:19; acc. re
  Impf. 3 ms. יְשֻׁלַּם ψ 65:2 Je 18:20; יְשֻׁלָּ֑ם Pr 11:31; 13:13;—
    be performed, of vow ψ 65:2.
    be repaid, requited, Je 18:20; Pr 11:31; 13:13.
    complete, perform: Impf. 3 ms. יַשְׁלִים Jb 23:14; Is 44:26, יַשְׁלִם v 28.
    make an end of, 2 ms. sf. תַּשְׁלִימֵנִי Is 38:12, 13 (𝔊 Du Marti deliver up to pains, as in Aramaic).

[85] ישליכו in Ezekiel 7:19: כַּסְפָּ֞ם בַּחוּצ֣וֹת יַשְׁלִ֗יכוּ וּזְהָבָם֮ לְנִדָּ֣ה יִֽהְיֶה֒ כַּסְפָּ֨ם וּזְהָבָ֜ם לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל לְהַצִּילָ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ עֶבְרַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֔ה נַפְשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְשַׂבֵּ֔עוּ וּמֵעֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּ֑אוּ כִּֽי־מִכְשׁ֥וֹל עֲוֺנָ֖ם הָיָֽה׃
(They shall throw their silver into the streets, and their gold shall be treated as something unclean. Their silver and gold shall not avail to save them in the day of GOD’s wrath—to satisfy their hunger or to fill their stomachs. Because they made them stumble into guilt—)

[86] שררך in Song of Songs 7:3: שׇׁרְרֵךְ֙ אַגַּ֣ן הַסַּ֔הַר אַל־יֶחְסַ֖ר הַמָּ֑זֶג בִּטְנֵךְ֙ עֲרֵמַ֣ת חִטִּ֔ים סוּגָ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
(Your navel is like a round goblet—Let mixed wine not be lacking!—Your belly like a heap of wheatHedged about with lilies.)
BDB שֹׁר²:
n.[m.] navel-string (cf. Aramaic שׁוּרָא Ez 16:4 𝔗, ܫܶܪܳܐ, Arabic سُرٌّ, all id.);—sf. לֹא כָרַּת שָׁרֵּךְ Ez 16:4 (Ges§ 22 s Kö ii. 1. 45) thy navel-string was

[87] שור in Exodus 21:36: א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְרֶ֖נּוּ בְּעָלָ֑יו שַׁלֵּ֨ם יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שׁוֹר֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּֽוֹ׃ {ס}        
(If, however, it is known that the ox was in the habit of goring, and its owner has failed to guard it, [that party] must restore ox for ox, but shall keep the dead animal.)

(the one responsible for the pit must make restitution—paying the price to the owner, but keeping the dead animal.)

params.system:
You help English-speaking learners of the Babylonian Talmud who tap a word of a Bible verse quoted in the Gemara and see its entry in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew lexicon (BDB). BDB entries are long; the page will open the entry at the sense that fits the word in this verse.

Each item gives the word as it stands in the verse, the verse (Hebrew, with an English translation), and an outline of the BDB entry: one line per sense (indented by depth), each cut to its first words. Lines that list forms ("Pf. 3 ms. ...", "Impf. ...") are not senses.

For each item:
- "q": copy, character for character, the first words (3 to 8) of the outline line where the sense that fits begins ("of animals Lv 11:39", "sometimes c. לְ pers. only = become the property of"). Point to the most specific sense that fits the word's plain meaning in this verse (pshat): the verse read on its own terms, as a Bible dictionary reads it, not as the Gemara expounds it. A participle used as a noun or adjective ("the dead one") fits the verb's sense for that subject (a dead animal: "of animals"). Use "" if only the entry's opening sense fits.
- "fit": "yes" if some sense fits the word's plain meaning in the verse; "no" if none does (the entry is probably the wrong one: another word spelled the same).

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: {"senses": {"<item id>": {"q": "...", "fit": "yes"}, ...}}
